correctness.rationale: The full-dimensional standard root polytope is an exact orthogonal product of a line segment and the image of the q-cross-polytope under vectors with Gram matrix I+J/2. All 2+2^q facets and their intrinsic normals follow from the invertible Gram matrix; its inverse is I-J/(q+2). Symmetric averaging makes the centered inball optimal, yielding radius (q-(q mod 2)/(q+2))^(-1/2) for q>=3. All maximal centers are forced by paired balanced-sign facet equalities; for odd q the active signs span all q dimensions, for even q precisely the sum-zero subspace. A strictly increasing scalar constraint gives both endpoints of the even-q center rectangle and all contact-facet equalities. This gives every quantifier/boundary in the claim. The complete package script independently enumerated exact sign norms in 3<=q<=70 and original-hull linear programs in 3<=q<=6; 6134 tests passed. Computation is corroboration only, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: One of the three recently characterized exceptional decomposable symmetric-edge families receives a complete metric solution, not merely a recomputation of its graph combinatorics. It includes the entire Euclidean facet-support distance multiset, a sharp radius, exact location and dimension of every maximum-ball center in all q>=3, parity-dependent line/rectangle geometry, and additional facet contacts at extremal centers. The quantitative sign-balance structure is motivated by the group-action decomposition and supplies information not implied by a known invariant table, with a natural indefinite parameter and no arbitrary slice.
